reference_answer: Parts of the Atacama Desert in Chile, with some weather stations recording decades without measurable rainfall.
notes: tests obscure but verifiable factual knowledge
model_response: The Atacama Desert in South America holds the record for the longest measured period without any recorded rainfall. Certain areas within this desert, particularly around Calama, Chile, went without a single drop of rain for an estimated 400 years until a storm occurred in 1971. Because of these extreme conditions, it is widely considered the driest non-polar desert on Earth.
